title: The scoreboard: what gets approved and what does not
question: Of everything that needed a special planning approval since 2015, how much was approved, refused or dropped, by kind of proposal?
finding: Of 5,392 applications decided since 2015, 73.1% were approved, 1.9% refused and 24.9% withdrawn or cancelled; the share not approved runs from 21.7% for new housing, 50 or more homes to 56.0% for removing or merging homes. Outright refusals are rare (104); most applications that fail are withdrawn. Of conditional-use requests filed in 2015-17, 32.2% were not approved; of those filed in 2021-23, 31.3% (variances: 27.8% and 31.5%). Projects of 10 or more homes moved most: 19.2% of 245 filed in 2015-18 were not approved and 39.5% of 124 filed in 2019-23 (84.4% of that later group has an outcome so far, and the ones still open are more likely to end in approval).
how: Every conditional-use, variance, large-project and historic-building application opened since 1 January 2015 in the Planning Department’s records, with the outcome the record states (approved; disapproved; withdrawn or cancelled). Each is sorted into one kind by the first rule that matches its own text and its parent project’s tick-boxes: New housing, 50 or more homes = the project adds 50 or more homes (net); New housing, 10 to 49 homes = adds 10 to 49 homes; Cannabis business = cannabis box ticked, or the words cannabis, marijuana or dispensary; Wireless antennas = the words wireless, antenna, telecommunication or small cell; Chain store (formula retail) = formula-retail box ticked or the words "formula retail"; New housing, 2 to 9 homes = adds 2 to 9 homes; Added in-law unit = in-law unit box ticked or the words accessory dwelling / ADU; One added home, or a new building with no home count given = adds one home, or the new-construction box is ticked with no unit count; Removing or merging homes = fewer homes after than before, or the words dwelling-unit removal / merger / unauthorized unit; Demolition = demolition box ticked or the word demolish; Restaurant, bar or entertainment = the words restaurant, bar, alcohol, liquor, entertainment, nightclub, brewery, tavern or cafe; School, child care, religious or medical = the words school, child care, church, religious, temple, hospital, medical, clinic or residential care; Office or hotel = the words office, hotel or motel; Sign or billboard = the words sign, signage, billboard or general advertising; Legalizing work already done = legalization box ticked or the word legalize; Addition or alteration to a building = additions or facade box ticked, or the words addition, expansion, rear yard, deck, dormer, garage, setback, facade, alteration; Change of use (other business) = change-of-use box ticked or the words change of use, establish, convert; Other or not stated = none of the above. Rates leave out 23 records closed with no outcome written and those still open. The two “filed” columns compare applications by the year they were filed, and the later one is blank unless at least 85% of that group has an outcome.
limits: A difference between places is not proof of bias. Places differ in what is proposed, in zoning, lot sizes, building ages and land prices, and in who chooses to apply at all; applicants also withdraw for their own reasons (money, a sale, a redesign filed under a new number). A withdrawal is the applicant’s act and the record does not say why; some are re-filed under a new number, and the department also closes stale files as withdrawn or cancelled, which can lift recent years. The keyword rules are rough and each case gets one label only. The hearing minutes, roll-call votes and appeal decisions now being collected would show who voted, who objected and what reason was recorded in each case.
